title: Encoding a signed-payload strkey with an empty payload must be refused
why: XDR allows a 0-byte payload but stellar-core rejects such a signer (CAP-0040), and strict strkey decoders refuse the text; an encoder that emits it produces an address its own decoder and the network refuse.

known_divergences.detail: Executed on v0.7.1: strkey.Encode emits PA7QYNF7…AAAAAAKH4Y for an empty payload, and its own decoder accepts the text too.
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 9E3 (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on go v0.7.1; xcc conform run --columns 'go@*' --entries 'strkey/api-encode-signed-payload-empty'

known_divergences.detail: Executed on v0.7.2, v0.7.3, v0.8.0 and v0.9.0: strkey.Encode emits PA7QYNF7…AAAAAAKH4Y for an empty payload, which the SDK's own decoder then refuses ('signed payload declares 0 payload bytes').
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 9E3 (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on go v0.7.2 and go v0.7.3 and go v0.8.0 and go v0.9.0; xcc conform run --columns 'go@*' --entries 'strkey/api-encode-signed-payload-empty'

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 28.0.0 and 28.0.1, which pin stellar-strkey 0.0.13: SignedPayload with an empty payload encodes to PA7QYNF7…AAAAAAKH4Y, which the library's own parser refuses. stellar-strkey 0.0.17 (#107) requires a non-empty payload; stellar-xdr 30.0.0 pins stellar-strkey 1.0.0 and refuses.
